title: AppShell
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigationsuite.NavigationSuiteScaffold, which puts androidx.compose.material3.NavigationBar, NavigationRail or a navigation drawer around the content for the window size
summary: The app shell is the Material 3 adaptive navigation container: NavigationSuiteScaffold shows a bottom navigation bar on a phone and a navigation rail on larger windows around the current destination. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: As the top level of an app with three to five main destinations, so the navigation adapts to phones, foldables, tablets and desktop windows by itself.
whenNotToUse: For an app with one main screen, use a Scaffold with a TopAppBar only. For more than five destinations, use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav). Inside a destination, use tabs for sections.
api: @Composable fun NavigationSuiteScaffold(navigationSuiteItems: NavigationSuiteScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layoutType: NavigationSuiteType = NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.calculateFromAdaptiveInfo(currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2()), navigationSuiteColors: NavigationSuiteColors = …, containerColor: Color = …, contentColor: Color = …, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

fun NavigationSuiteScope.item(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, alwaysShowLabel: Boolean = true, badge: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, …)

appearance: The bar and the rail use the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the raised surface, the accent subtle color for the selected indicator and the muted text color for the other destinations. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web AppShell lays out a rail, an identity bar and the main region, and adds a skip link, landmarks and contained scrolling. On Android the navigation suite does the layout and adapts to the window; there are no landmarks or skip links to add: TalkBack moves between the navigation and the content, and each destination scrolls on its own. The web's identity bar becomes the actions of each destination's TopAppBar, such as an account menu. iOS uses TabView. The catalogue page shows the bar and the rail with plain layout because the sample app does not depend on the navigation suite library; the example uses the real NavigationSuiteScaffold.
accessibility: System behavior: each destination is a selectable item; TalkBack reads its label, its selected state and its badge.
Each item has a touch target of at least 48dp.
Keep a label on every item (alwaysShowLabel = true), so a destination is never named by its icon alone.
Icons are decorative (contentDescription = null) because the label names the destination.
edgeCases: Keep each destination's state with rememberSaveable or a view model: the suite recomposes the content when the window changes size.
A badge with a count should also be said in the label or the item's semantics when it matters, such as "Inbox, 3 unread".
